segments: The Chronography of Bar Hebraeus.
Then {OCR?} the forces of the Arabs crossed over after them,
and became a barrier between them and the water,
while others were in front of them.
And they remained in the middle, tormented by hunger and thirst together with their horses.
And the Arabs took courage and struck them with a very great blow,
and killed the majority of them,
and bound the king and the nobles, and brought him to al-Mu'azzam,
who imprisoned him with him where he was encamped.
Then the young slaves, his contemporaries, advised al-Mu'azzam and said to him:
"If you kill this Frankish king,
all the days of your life you will not have relief from war with the Franks,
because their kings are many,
and they are mighty in their power.
Rather, make this one swear
that from now until one hundred and twenty years, neither he, nor his brothers, nor their sons, nor their sons' sons, will again draw swords against the Arabs.
And let him go,
so that he may acknowledge your favor among the people of his faith.
And in this way you will rest and live in peace,
and you will not need to squander the treasures that your fathers laid up for the forces."
And al-Mu'azzam was persuaded by their counsel,
and brought the King of France to him by night,
and made him swear as he wished,
and gave him many gifts and released him.
It is said
that during the days when the King of France was imprisoned,
news came to him
that the queen, his wife, had borne him a son in Damietta.
And al-Mu'azzam heard [of this],
and sent her gifts of ten thousand red dinars,
and a golden cradle with royal garments.
However, the old slaves of his father, as soon as they perceived that al-Mu'azzam had released the King of France, became enraged,
and sent ships on the sea to capture him.
And when they did not overtake him,
they drew swords and fell upon al-Mu'azzam.
And he fled before them,
and went up into a wooden tower {burj} which he had.
And they set fire to the tower.
And when he saw himself caught by the fire,
he threw himself into the sea and was drowned,
and his corpse was never found at all.
The King of France, however, brought out all his people from Damietta and came to Acre,
and resided in it for some time.
And he rebuilt Caesarea Philippi
and other cities,
and left and went to his country.
